title: Keeping only some of the values
idea: Opener: the idea of a filter — walk a list and keep only the items that pass a test. Thinking first, no new syntax.

exercises.prompt: You have the scores [4, 9, 2, 7, 5] and you want only the scores above 5. Which numbers do you keep?
exercises.explanation: You keep each number that passes the test 'above 5'. Only 9 and 7 pass. That 'keep the ones that pass' idea is called filtering.

options: going through every item and keeping only the ones that pass a test
exercises.explanation: A filter walks the whole list and keeps the items that match a condition. The rest are simply left out.

exercises.prompt: When you filter a list, the items you keep go into a NEW list — the original list is not changed.
exercises.explanation: Filtering builds a fresh, shorter list of the ones that passed. The original stays as it was, which is handy if you still need it.

exercises.prompt: From [12, 3, 20, 8, 1] you want only the numbers below 10. What does the kept list contain?
exercises.explanation: Test each one against 'below 10'. 3, 8 and 1 pass; 12 and 20 do not. The kept list is [3, 8, 1].

exercises.prompt: Which everyday task is most like filtering a list?
options: Picking only the ripe apples out of a basket
Counting how many apples there are
Stacking the apples in a tower
exercises.explanation: Picking only the ripe ones is a filter: you check each apple and keep the ones that pass 'is it ripe?'.

exercises.prompt: You filter [2, 5, 8, 11, 14] for 'even numbers'. Which numbers end up in the kept list? (Pick all.)
exercises.explanation: Even means it divides by 2 with no remainder. 2, 8 and 14 are even; 5 and 11 are odd and are left out.

exercises.prompt: A filter can keep NONE of the items if nothing passes the test.
exercises.explanation: If no item passes, the kept list is empty — that is a perfectly normal result, not an error.

exercises.prompt: To decide whether to keep an item, what do you need first?
options: A test (a true/false condition) to check each item against
The total of all the items
exercises.explanation: Filtering always needs a test that is either true or false for each item, like 'is it above 5?'. The true ones are kept.

exercises.prompt: Put the plain-English steps of a filter in order.
blocks: For each item, check it against the test
If it passes, add it to the kept list
After the loop, the kept list holds the matches
exercises.explanation: Start empty, walk every item, add the ones that pass, and when the loop ends the kept list is your answer. This is the shape of every filter.

exercises.prompt: You already know how to walk a list and test an item. What is the one NEW thing a filter does with the items that pass?
options: It collects them into a new list
It prints the whole original list
It counts how many there are in total
exercises.explanation: You know the loop and the if-test already. The new move is collecting the passers into a fresh list — you'll do exactly that next lesson.
